messages:
alex: FYI ran nightly compaction on redwood-canary-3 and observed a weird slab collapse on node5, caused an eviction spike and hitrate drop. attaching quick notes.

alex: short logs: 
```
[2026-03-16T03:12:15Z] compaction:start cohort=slab aggressive=1
[2026-03-16T03:18:02Z] eviction:bulk node=node5 rate=23.4%
[2026-03-16T03:18:03Z] hitrate:window=5m before=0.87 after=0.64
[2026-03-16T03:18:05Z] latency:p99 before=12ms after=48ms
```

maria: ouch. can you paste the bench command you ran and the commit SHA for the runtime?

alex: command was:
```
run_kv_bench --cohort=slab --compaction=aggressive --seed=42 --duration=30m --target=redwood-canary-3 --clients=200
```
runtime SHA: 4f9b2c8 (deployed last night via canary pipeline)

jing: can you also capture a pprof/heap and flamegraph from node5? we need to know whether the eviction is to free small objects or a large KV fragment collapse.

alex: yep, started a pprof on node5 at 03:19. here's the pid snapshot reference: /tmp/profiles/node5-2065432100.tar.gz (uploading to the artifacts bucket now)

sourav: quick thought — aggressive compaction + slab reclamation threshold at 0.2 might cause coalescing which invalidates some prefix references. check runtime config `kv.slab.reclaim_threshold`. you might want to try 0.5 as a control.

alex: current on canary is 0.2. will flip to 0.5 for a compare run.

sam: can we repro in a smaller env? i'd like a synthetic workload that reproduces the fragment alignment issue without hitting production-ish traffic. suggest: clients=40, keyspace=500k, skew=zipf(1.1), compaction=aggressive, duration=10m.

alex: starting that on sandbox-4 now, will post numbers in ~12m.

infra-bot: ALERT: redwood-canary-3 node5 reported OOM-kill event at 2026-03-16T03:18:08Z. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood.local/INC-2065

maria: thanks — if there's an OOM kill, we should capture kernel OOM logs and core dumps too. alex, can you run the same bench with `--pprof=on --dump-occupancy=kv_map`? the occupancy map will help us see fragmentation.

alex: will do. scheduling second run now with `--pprof=on --dump-occupancy=kv_map --reclaim_threshold=0.5`

jing: also throw `--collect-hot-keys=1m` so we can verify whether hotset shifted during compaction.

alex: added. pinging @maria @sourav for a quick CR on the small runtime change I pushed to gate the aggressive compaction behind a flag (opt-in). would like eyes before flipping on the canary. :eyes:

maria: taking a look now. if we gate it behind `kv.compaction.aggressive_enabled` and default to false in prod flags, sound safe. i'll leave comments in PR.

sourav: sg, also add a metric for `compaction_overlap_seconds` so we can alert on long-running overlaps of compaction + heavy request windows.

alex: good idea, adding it to the PR.

sam: sandbox run finished — small repro reproduced hitrate dip but no OOM. numbers: before compaction hr=0.88, during=0.69, eviction rate peak=12.1%, p99=36ms. artifacts: s3://ci-artifacts/kvt/sandbox-2065432100/*

jing: can you attach the flamegraph link?

sam: flamegraph uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.local/flamegraphs/sandbox-2065432100.svg

alex: thanks. next steps: (1) wait for canary pprof upload to finish, (2) run the same sandbox config with prefetch disabled to check prefetch vs compaction interference, (3) hold canary rollback if OOM persists. I'll update this thread when the occupancy dump is ready.

maria: add a brief note to the incident ticket summarizing the sandbox repro and that a patch/flag is in review.

ajing: (small follow) @alex can you include a snapshot of `kv.slot_fragmentation_percent` from metrics during the window? we want a numeric baseline for trend alerts.

alex: posted the metric snapshot to the incident: 
```
kv.slot_fragmentation_percent{node="node5"} = 42.3 at 03:17, 78.9 at 03:19
```

alex: occupancy dump upload done: s3://ci-artifacts/kvt/occupancy-node5-2065432100.json.gz

alex: tagging this for follow-up in next week's eng-runtime sync; will propose a small guardrail change (reclaim_threshold default bump + overlap metric) and link the PR in case anyone wants to review earlier.

maria: thanks — nice quick triage. :thumbsup:

alex: @sourav want to own the rollout guardrail? if yes i'll add you to PR as approver.

sourav: happy to. will review the PR today and validate on sandbox/qa before prod canary.

alex: cool. closing the loop here for now, will post any new artifacts in this thread.
